title: TLAC Impact Report 2026: From a Single Classroom to an Entire System
author: Teach Like a Champion Team
summary: Teach Like a Champion's inaugural Impact Report (2026) documents what happens when schools embed TLAC classroom techniques into long-term professional development infrastructure rather than deploying them as standalone interventions. The report draws on partnerships with districts including Harmony Public Schools (Texas), Amarillo ISD, and others to show that systemic integration produces sustained, measurable gains. Harmony outperformed the Texas state average by 67 points after anchoring leadership actions in Core 4 capacities across 60 campuses. At Travis Middle School in Amarillo — where 97% of students are economically disadvantaged — 6th-grade math classes posted a 25-percentage-point STAAR gain after TLAC-aligned coaching. A Science of Reading cohort saw median student fluency jump from a dysfluent 96 WCPM to a fluent 137 WCPM, crossing the critical comprehension threshold through FASE Reading routines and video-based reflection. The unifying finding: the same techniques that transform individual classrooms produce exponential results when woven into a school or network's development architecture over multiple years.
points: Embedding TLAC techniques into a district's long-term professional development infrastructure — rather than delivering them as one-off workshops — produces sustainable academic growth across entire networks of schools.

Harmony Public Schools (Texas), serving 42,000 students across 60 campuses, outperformed the Texas state average by 67 points after building a unified instructional vocabulary and anchoring leadership in Core 4 capacities.

At Travis Middle School in Amarillo ISD — where 97% of students are economically disadvantaged — 6th-grade math classes posted a 25-percentage-point STAAR gain following TLAC-aligned lesson preparation and coaching feedback cycles.

Oral reading fluency below 110 WCPM consumes working memory with decoding, leaving little capacity for comprehension; a Science of Reading cohort moved median student fluency from 96 WCPM to 137 WCPM through FASE Reading routines.
Teacher quality remains the single most important school-related factor in student achievement, whether improvement is unlocked through a single workshop, new curriculum, or a multi-year partnership.
